messages:
incident-bot: Pager received: elevated 5xx spike on /v1/generate (gateway 502/504) — pages: ryan_oncall. CP severity: high. Estimated customer impact: multiple small requests failing with retries. Correlation hint: header X-Request-ID present.
ryan_oncall: on it, joining. any idea if it's regional?
ash_sre: I see error rate spike from gateway in eu-west-1 starting ~2167776000, spreading to us-central after ~120s. Upstream service reports increased 502 from runtime-proxy.
lina_prod: support ticket stream shows ~120 customers with transient failures; a few high-volume customers retried aggressively (10-30 rps each).
simone_eng: can we confirm if gateway is returning 502 vs timeout? logs?
ash_sre: quick grep shows both. sample lines: ```[2026-02-14T10:40:12Z] gateway TRACE id=cid:abc123 status=502 upstream=runtime-proxy error="upstream reset" pid=22
[2026-02-14T10:40:13Z] gateway TRACE id=cid:abc124 status=504 upstream=router error="deadline" pid=22```
jen_support: customers reporting last 10m errors: 502 then retries, some got successful response after retries. ticket snippets attached.
ryan_oncall: mitigation plan (short): 1) add temporary routing fallback to smaller model variant for heavy customers, 2) increase gateway upstream timeout from 10s -> 15s for the route, 3) rate-limit the heavy API keys to slow retry amplification. Thoughts?
ash_sre: +1 on rate-limit. I'm worried about connection pool exhaustion at proxy->runtime. Need to inspect connection reuse metrics.
simone_eng: I'll pull kv logs and tail runtime pod stderr. sharing grep command: `kubectl logs -f runtime-proxy-*-pod -c runtime | grep --line-buffered "cid:abc"`
ash_sre: found a pattern: a subset of requests are getting long queue latency before being forwarded. timeline bucket: 10:39:50 - 10:41:30 queue latency > 2s, then upstream reset. Could be backlog.
lina_prod: customer impact: some interactive chat sessions had partial responses; flagging enterprise customer ACME-1 as high-touch. contacting AE now.
ryan_oncall: I'm going to apply rate-limit to top offending keys via admin route. I'll post config diff.
ryan_oncall: `POST /admin/keys/rate_limit { key: "acme-1", max_rps: 2 }` -> applied.
deploy-bot: config-change: rate-limit applied to key acme-1 by ryan_oncall at 2026-02-14T10:46:03Z :white_check_mark:
ash_sre: immediate improvement in gateway queue length after rate-limit. 502s dropping for acme-1 requests. aggregate 5xx rate dropped ~40% in 60s.
simone_eng: sharing raw log snippet for a problematic correlation id: ```... id=cid:xyz789 request="POST /v1/generate" latency_queue=2200ms latency_upstream=120ms upstream_status=502 message="connection reset by peer" trace=/traces/xyz789 ```
ryan_oncall: that looks like backlog + upstream reset. hypothesis A: runtime-proxy threadpool exhausted leading to abrupt connection resets. hypothesis B: an upstream worker crashed under load, causing immediate resets for in-flight connections.
jen_support: ACME-1 says they saw retries bumping to 200 rps because client SDK auto-retries on 5xx. Could be exacerbating.
ash_sre: checking runtime pod restarts: there are 2 restarts of runtime-proxy in the 10:38-10:42 window on node n2-az1. kube events show OOMKilled? No, logs show 'goroutine stack dump' preceding exit. copying excerpt: ```panic: runtime error: out of memory
... goroutine 123 [running]:
```
simone_eng: ok that's telling. OOM -> worker restart -> upstream connection resets -> gateway 502s -> clients retry -> cascade. mitigation: add temporary instance capacity and lower per-client concurrency.
ryan_oncall: I'm spinning up two extra runtime-proxy replicas in eu-west-1 now. `kubectl scale deployment runtime-proxy -n prod --replicas=6`
ash_sre: also we should patch the gateway to fail-fast when upstream queue > X to avoid queueing. I'm adding a quick rule to deny requests when queue depth > 250.
simone_eng: scaling up replicas succeeded; initial CPU/mem pressure dropping, restarts stopped. 5xx rate returning toward baseline.
lina_prod: ACME-1 confirms errors dropped on their side after the rate-limit and scaling. They still want a postmortem.
jen_support: adding impacted customers list to the incident doc and opening follow-up tickets for billing credits where appropriate.
ryan_oncall: for RCA in-thread: timeline, hypothesis, evidence, mitigation, follow-ups. I'll start timeline draft: 10:38:30 first queue latency spike; 10:39:00 runtime-proxy OOM and restart; 10:39:20 upstream connection resets => gateway 502 spike; 10:44:00 rate-limit applied to acme-1; 10:46:03 additional replicas scaled; 10:50:00 error rate back to baseline.
nash_sre: evidence items: kube events (oomkiller), pod logs (stack dump + OOM panic), gateway logs with correlation ids (sampled), customer ticket list. adding links: /incidents/2167777888/k8s-events, /incidents/2167777888/gateway-logs, /traces/xyz789
simone_eng: long-term actions: 1) tune runtime-proxy memory settings + better request shedding, 2) add client-side retry guidance & SDK update to jitter/backoff, 3) autoscale policy based on queue depth, not just CPU.
ryan_oncall: agree. I'll create JIRA tickets for those with owners. tagging @ash_sre for memory tuning, @simone_eng to own autoscale policy, @lina_prod to coordinate customer comms.
nash_sre: one more ask: capture a set of correlation ids to attach to the postmortem for trace replays. I have list: [cid:abc123, cid:abc124, cid:xyz789, cid:def456].
jen_support: adding those to the incident doc. Also logging timeline entry for customer comms.
ryan_oncall: closing mitigation loop: system stable, no ongoing OOMs. We'll keep monitoring for 1 hour then wrap. Creating postmortem draft now.
incident-bot: Incident transitioned: mitigation -> monitoring, severity downgraded to medium. Pager cleared for ryan_oncall.
simone_eng: quick note for postmortem: include a small snippet of the failing stack dump (sanitized), and the exact kube resource limits current vs recommended.
ryan_oncall: thanks all — good cross-team response. I'll ping again once postmortem is ready for review.
jen_support: pushing customer comms draft to the incident doc. :thumbsup:
